title: AGENTS.md Review Policy: 4 Sections CodeRabbit, Copilot, and Claude Code All Read

title: PHP2Shell: Your Host Patched PHP. Your Site Might Still Be Exposed.
summary:
Your web host patched PHP. Your WordPress is up to date. Your plugins are up to date.
That does not mean your site is patched.

On October 21, PHP shipped emergency fixes for two critical bugs now called PHP2Shell.
I've run a crowdsourcing platform in Japan for 22 years, and on the night the fixes came out I was doing emergency work on my clients' sites.
Two weeks later, a lot more is known: who actually got hit, why the version number on your dashboard can be misleading, and what to look for in your logs.

I also made a video about this.

title: CodeSOD: Only Create Me if I Exist
summary:
Foreign keys are an important part of making sure the entities in our relational database can be connected back together and queried correctly. It's part of proper data normalization. This isn't shocking, of course: the order line table has a foreign key over to the products table, so that every line item points to a product we sell. That's database 101. Database 201, you'd also think about the times where you have a hierarchy of records, where say, every Employee has a ManagerId, which is a foreign key back to the Employee table itself (and in database 301, you'll understand why having a ManagerId field is a terrible choice, but that's neither here nor there).

The important thing here is that foreign keys are very common, and foreign keys pointing back to the same table are also very common.

But it can still go very wrong. Roman sends us this foreign key definition in a database they maintain.
